method.population: cleaned rows whose measurement field carries at least one digit and whose candidate rule fires
method.false_positive_test: support_text names an absolute PK parameter (Km|Ki|IC50|EC50|Kd|Papp|Vmax|CL|AUC|Cmax|Kp|clearance) and contains no relative marker (fold|%|percent|compared|versus|vs|relative|probability|ratio|higher|lower)
method.note: The test is a lower bound on false positives: it only counts rows whose absolute quantity is named in the support text.

examples: Km = 1448 uM, Vmax = 624 pmol/min/mg protein (BCECF in BBM)

reasoning: These columns record the conclusion a study drew -- substrate status, inhibitor status, comparative framing -- not whether a quantity was measured. A paper may report IC50 = 0.51 uM and still conclude only that the compound is an inhibitor, so qualitative evidence and an absolute number coexist freely. The non-scalar bucket discards a row with no extraction pass behind it, so any nonzero false-positive rate silently deletes evidence. The DeclarativeNonScalarRule mechanism is retained for columns that describe the measurement itself, such as bioavailability's bioavailability_report_type == 'relative_comparison'.

columns_excluded_without_measurement.direct_bbb.bbb_permeability_label: outcome interpretation; a permeable compound still has a reported Papp
